# Minimum enclosing simplices: attained facet-centroid contacts and locality

Let K be a full-dimensional compact convex body in R^m, m>=1.
There exists a minimum-volume enclosing simplex S. EVERY such
minimizer has the property

    the centroid of every facet of S belongs to K.  (1)

No differentiability or strict convexity of K is required. Moreover
the construction is local near a reference simplex in an explicit
sense. Let T=conv(0,e_1,...,e_m). If

    dist_H,infinity(K,T)<=delta<=1/(8m^2),

then EVERY minimum-volume enclosing simplex satisfies

    dist_H,infinity(S,T)<=8m^3 delta.              (2)

If delta<=1/(64m^3), its vertices can be labeled a_0,...,a_m
corresponding to 0,e_1,...,e_m so that

    max_i ||a_i-v_i||_infinity<=8m^3 delta.         (3)

Consequently the retained facet-centroid contacts in (1), with
the corresponding labeling, lie within 8m^3 delta of the facet
centroids of T. These are ordinary convex-geometric statements;
no lattice change or mixed-measure conclusion is involved.

## 1. Attainment, including the exclusion of escaping vertices

Fix one enclosing simplex of volume V_0 and an inscribed Euclidean
ball B(x_0,r) contained in K, r>0. Consider a minimizing sequence
of enclosing simplices of volume at most V_0. Every vertex v of
each such simplex obeys

    |v-x_0|<=m V_0/[kappa_(m-1) r^(m-1)],          (4)

where kappa_(m-1) is the volume of the unit (m-1)-ball (kappa_0=1).
Indeed, take the equatorial (m-1)-disk of B(x_0,r) in the plane
through x_0 perpendicular to v-x_0. The cone from this disk to
v is contained in the simplex and has volume
kappa_(m-1)r^(m-1)|v-x_0|/m. This proves (4), also for m=1.

Label the m+1 vertices arbitrarily in each simplex. Boundedness
and a subsequence give simultaneous convergence of all vertices.
Their convex hulls converge in Hausdorff distance to the convex
hull of the limiting vertices. This limit contains K: for each
fixed point of K its distance to every hull is zero. Since K is
full-dimensional, the m+1 limiting vertices are affinely independent.
The limit is therefore a full-dimensional enclosing simplex.
The determinant volume formula is continuous in its vertices,
so its volume equals the infimum. This proves attainment without
a compactness assumption on an unbounded parameter space.

## 2. Every facet supports K

Let S be a minimizer and F one of its facets. If its supporting
hyperplane missed K, compactness would give positive distance
between K and that plane. Move the plane slightly inwards, holding
the other m planes fixed. Their common vertex opposite F stays
fixed; for a sufficiently small move the intersection remains a
bounded full-dimensional simplex containing K, with strictly smaller
volume. This contradiction shows F intersect K is nonempty.

Equivalently, after an affine map sending S to the standard simplex
and F to sum x_i=1, the other facets are x_i>=0. Replacing the
last inequality by sum x_i<=1-epsilon is feasible for small
epsilon>0 if F misses K, and multiplies the volume by
(1-epsilon)^m. This also treats m=1.

## 3. A facet tilt forces its centroid into the contact set

Keep the same affine coordinates for a selected facet:

    S={x_i>=0, sum_i x_i<=1},
    F={x_i>=0, sum_i x_i=1},
    g_F=(1/m,...,1/m).

Suppose g_F is not in K. Its compact convex contact set
C=K intersect F is nonempty by Section 2, and g_F is not in C.
Strict separation supplies a linear functional v dot x and a
real s with

    max_(x in C) v dot x < s < v dot g_F.          (5)

We claim that, for every sufficiently small epsilon>0, the new
facet inequality

    sum_i x_i-1+epsilon(v dot x-s)<=0              (6)

still contains ALL of K. This is a compactness argument with an
actual uniform margin, not differentiation of a support function.
By (5), v dot x-s<0 on a relative neighborhood in K of C.
There exists eta>0 such that this inequality remains strictly
negative on {x in K: sum x_i-1>=-eta}; otherwise a convergent
sequence would contradict (5). On the remaining compact part
sum x_i-1<=-eta, while |v dot x-s| is bounded. Taking epsilon
small makes (6) hold there too. This proves feasibility.

Keeping x_i>=0 fixed, (6) defines the simplex

    sum_i (1+epsilon v_i)x_i<=1+epsilon s.

For small epsilon both the right side and all m coefficients
are positive. Its volume is exactly

    |S| (1+epsilon s)^m / product_i(1+epsilon v_i).

Its derivative at zero is

    |S|[m s-sum_i v_i]
      =m|S|[s-v dot g_F]<0,                       (7)

contradicting minimum volume. Hence g_F belongs to K. Affine maps
preserve facet centroids and multiply all volumes by a constant,
so the conclusion holds in the original coordinates. This proves
(1) for every facet and every minimizing simplex, including
nonsmooth or positive-dimensional contact sets.

No Lagrange multiplier qualification is required: (5)-(7) give
an explicit feasible descent whenever the asserted contact fails.

## 4. Explicit locality from inner and outer simplices

Suppose dist_H,infinity(K,T)<=delta with 0<delta<=1/(8m^2).
Support-function comparison gives

    T_-={x_i>=delta, sum x_i<=1-m delta} subset K,
    K subset T_+={x_i>=-delta, sum x_i<=1+m delta}. (8)

For the first inclusion, T_-+[-delta,delta]^m is contained in T,
and h_K(u)>=h_T(u)-delta||u||_1. This implies h_(T_-)<=h_K.
The second follows directly from Hausdorff distance. The two
simplices have volumes

    |T_-|=(1-2m delta)^m |T|,
    |T_+|=(1+2m delta)^m |T|.                      (9)

Any minimizing S contains T_- and has volume at most |T_+|.
Set

    Delta=[(1+2m delta)^m-(1-2m delta)^m]
                                      /(1-2m delta)^(m-1),
    E=Delta-delta.                                (10)

We claim EVERY point x in S satisfies

    x_i>=delta-Delta=-E,
    sum x_i<=1-m delta+Delta<=1+E.                (11)

For a point with x_i<delta, the cone from x to the facet
{x_i=delta} of T_- is contained in S and has interior disjoint
from T_-. Its volume is

    |T| (delta-x_i)(1-2m delta)^(m-1).

Comparing |S| with (9) proves delta-x_i<=Delta. For the top
facet, the same cone argument gives volume

    |T| [sum x_i-(1-m delta)](1-2m delta)^(m-1)

whenever the bracket is positive. The Euclidean facet area has
a factor sqrt(m), which cancels the factor 1/sqrt(m) in the
height. This proves (11). For m=1 the argument is the ordinary
length of an interval appended beyond an endpoint.

The elementary bounds needed below are

    4m^2 delta<=Delta<=8m^2 delta,
    E>=m delta.                                   (12)

The lower bound follows by retaining the linear term in the
positive odd-binomial expansion of the numerator and using
(1-2m delta)^(m-1)<=1. For the upper bound, the mean-value
theorem bounds the numerator by
4m^2 delta(1+2m delta)^(m-1). Write a=2m delta<=1/(4m).
Bernoulli gives (1-a)^(m-1)>=3/4, while
(1+a)^(m-1)<=1/[1-(m-1)a]<=4/3, by comparing its binomial
coefficients with the geometric series. Their ratio is at most
16/9<2. This proves the upper bound; E>=m delta follows from
4m^2-1>=m for m>=1.

By (11), S is contained in the homothetic outer simplex

    T_E={x_i>=-E, sum x_i<=1+E}
       =-E 1+[1+(m+1)E]T.

Every point of T_E is within mE in infinity norm of its
corresponding point of T. Conversely, every T point is within
delta of K and hence of S. Equations (10)-(12) therefore give

    dist_H,infinity(S,T)<=max(delta,mE)<=8m^3 delta,

which is (2). The argument actually applies to any convex
enclosing body of volume at most |T_+|; minimization is used only
to obtain that volume upper bound.

## 5. Vertex and facet matching

Assume further delta<=1/(64m^3). For each i>=1 select a vertex
a_i of S maximizing coordinate x_i. Since K approximates e_i,
x_i(a_i)>=1-delta. Equations (11) imply

    |x_i(a_i)-1|<=max(delta,mE),
    -E<=x_j(a_i)<=delta+(m-1)E<=mE, j!=i.

Choose a vertex a_0 minimizing sum x_i. Since K approximates
the origin, sum x_i(a_0)<=m delta. Thus

    -E<=x_i(a_0)<=m delta+(m-1)E<=mE,

where the last inequality uses E>=m delta. Every selected a_i
lies within mE<=8m^3 delta<=1/8 of its respective standard
vertex. These m+1 neighborhoods are disjoint, so these are
distinct vertices. A simplex has exactly m+1 vertices; hence
they list all its vertices and prove (3).

The centroid of the facet opposite a_i is the average of the
other m vertices. It is therefore within the same bound of the
centroid of the corresponding facet of T. Section 3 says this
point is an actual K contact. No continuity theorem for facet
normals or combinatorial approximation of K was assumed.

If delta=0, K=T. An enclosing simplex has volume at least |T|,
and equality forces it to equal T: any additional point yields
a positive cone beyond some supporting facet of T. Thus all
statements include this endpoint as well.

## 6. Scope and relation to the edge-union route

The attained centroids provide all facets simultaneously with
actual retained points at their precise barycentric centers.
This avoids assuming that arbitrary nearby supporting planes
have centered contacts. It does not by itself give a depth or
missing-volume inequality; those require a separate estimate.

The earlier bounded edge result is preserved in
tetrahedron-thin-edge-unions-and-facet-layer-limit.md. It proves
coverage <=3/2 for arbitrary edge-cap unions in a genuinely thin
edge tube, and gives an exact near-tetrahedron facet-layer example
showing why such tube localization does not follow from small
missing volume alone. The present contact lemma makes no such
localization assumption.

## 7. Exact verification

The standard-library verifier
../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_minimum_enclosing_simplex_contacts_locality.py passes 95
actual full-dimensional source/feasible-tilt examples, 280 exact
dimensional locality and cone-budget checks, and 123 vertex/facet
matching cases, covering dimensions 1 through 40. It verifies
the determinant ratio, strict volume descent, and every numerical
constant in (10)-(12). These checks supplement the proofs above;
in particular they do not substitute for the compactness and
uniform feasibility arguments in Sections 1 and 3.
